Synopsis:
The player tries to read a bronze plaque at the foot of an unidentified statue.

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_OutsideStatue.json: The player is standing inside a tomb chamber before a statue with a worn bronze plaque at its base, having likely reached this room after navigating the tomb’s corridors and hazards. The plaque’s inscription is obscured by age—fading, grime, corrosion, poor lighting, or an unfamiliar script—so the game often requires an Investigation/Perception or language/lore check to make out the words. Companions, scholars, or an unseen narrator may offer translations, lore, warnings, or practical help (or note that the text is illegible). Reading the plaque could reveal names, dates, rituals, or clues relevant to the tomb and may advance quest text or trigger a reaction from the environment.
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_SqueletonRoom.json: The player reads a bronze plaque at the feet of a mysterious statue
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_TrappedTomb.json: The scene takes place inside a tomb where the player is examining a bronze plaque whose inscription is in an unfamiliar script. The narrator explicitly notes the text is a mystery, so off-screen the party lacks the means (knowledge, a scholar, or a translation spell) to read it. The player's spoken line is a speculative inference that the inscription refers to an ancient cult or deity, not a revealed fact.
- CHA_BronzePlaque_AD_SanctumStatue.json: You are standing inside a tomb before a worn bronze plaque set at the feet of an unidentified statue, trying to make out an inscription obscured by grime, corrosion, or an unfamiliar script. The plaque’s language may be unknown to you — the narration or your character can note you “do not recognise” it — so the game often requires an Investigation/Perception or language/lore check to decipher it. If companions or an NPC scholar are present they might offer translations or commentary (or a narrator might give a brief rendering); otherwise the text may be presented as an interpreted description. The plaque likely contains names, dates, warnings, ritual details, or clues relevant to the tomb and reading it can advance knowledge, trigger quest text, or provoke an environmental reaction; the player’s line can be skeptical or mocking while speculating about a dedication to a forgotten god.
- CHA_Crypt_VB_Sanctum_2_WithShadowheart.json: Players have entered an abandoned chapel dedicated to an unknown god. Shadowheart is puzzled as to why she can't figure out who was the patron of this place.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Player: Text is too faded. Doesn't tell me who was worshipped here. || [context] NodeContext: Players with religious classes comment on the plaque. (node 0)

Sample 2:
- Narrator: *Time and the elements have left the plaque unreadable.* || [context] NodeContext: Narrator describes an illegible plaque. (node 1)

context: You’re standing in a tomb chamber before an unidentified statue with a worn bronze plaque set at its feet, having reached this room after navigating the tomb’s corridors and hazards. The plaque’s inscription is obscured by age — fading, grime, corrosion, or an unfamiliar script — so the game typically requires an Investigation/Perception check or a language/lore/translation source to make out the words. If no companion scholar or translation spell is present, the narrator (or companions) may simply note the text is unreadable, and the player’s lines often become speculative remarks rather than factual readings. Reading the plaque, if deciphered, can reveal names, dates, warnings or ritual clues relevant to the tomb and may advance quest text or provoke an environmental reaction.
